subject: SLA crediting, canary escalation, and packaging options
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Alyssa Park <alyssa@luminorhealth.com>, Tom Nguyen <tnguyen@luminorhealth.com>
Date: 2026-04-15T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: SLA crediting, canary escalation, and packaging options

Hi Alyssa / Tom —

Thanks again for the time today. Per our call I wanted to put a concise starting point on the table so you can share with finance/ops. Attached: 'slo_matrix_v2.xlsx' (uplift bands / uptime credit examples) and 'canary_plan.pdf' (short runbook for canary failover and rollback).

High-level proposal:
- Uptime tiers: 99.9% (standard), 99.95% (guaranteed), 99.99% (enterprise)
- Response windows: P2 (4h), P1 (1h) for enterprise; can push to 30m on staffed retainer
- Crediting: sliding credits by month when below target (0.5% / 1% / 2% of monthly invoice by tier)
- Escalation: 24/7 on-call escalation for enterprise with named on-call and quarterly runbooks

Two asks from your side we wanted to validate: 1) target months for a price lock (12 vs 36 months), 2) appetite for a modest seat commitment to subsidize faster response lanes.

If you confirm 36 months + 50 committed seats we can propose a dual concession: 5% committed discount + a 20% uplift on crediting caps (i.e., higher max credit but narrower response windows). Otherwise we have a standard 12-month path with a smaller concession.

Next steps: if it looks OK I can send a dashed proposal and a DocuSign for signature by early next week.

Thanks,
Jonas Weber
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0142

Attachments: slo_matrix_v2.xlsx, canary_plan.pdf

From: Alyssa Park <alyssa@luminorhealth.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Nguyen <tnguyen@luminorhealth.com>
Date: 2026-04-15T09:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SLA crediting, canary escalation, and packaging options

Jonas —

Appreciate the recap. A few clarifications from Luminor:
- We lean toward 36 months if the unit economics are locked and there's a clear runbook for failover.
- We need P1 to be 30 minutes for core patient-facing endpoints; P2 at 4 hours is fine for batch/analytics.
- Can you outline how credits interact with our monthly committed spend (we want to avoid revenue volatility).

Also important: procurement will ask for evidence of on-call escalation (named roster + SLA contacts) and a simple 30-day exit clause tied to a critical regression.

Tom and I will review materials and come back with one list of redlines.

Best,
Alyssa Park
Director of Platform Reliability, Luminor Health
alyssa@luminorhealth.com

Marissa / Priyom —

Forwarding Alyssa's reply from Luminor. They want P1=30m for patient-facing endpoints and are leaning 36 months if we give stronger credit caps and named on-call evidence. Procurement will push for a 30-day critical regression exit clause — can we accept or propose a compromise?

Two quick asks: 1) Priyom, can you draft a conservative credits table that avoids revenue volatility while giving them comfort (I attached our starter 'proposed_pricing_sheet.xlsx' as a stub), 2) Marissa, can you confirm whether we can provide a named quarterly on-call roster + blackout exceptions for a 36-month commit?

If we can do 5% commit discount + a staged credit uplift (cap increases in year 2/3) we should be able to land this. Also thinking a signed canary runbook as a precondition for 30m P1.

Thanks —
Jonas

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-04-16T11:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: SLA crediting, canary escalation, and packaging options

Jonas / Priyom —

Notes after quick review and ops sync:
- Named on-call: yes, we can provide a quarterly roster and a single escalation contact for legal to reference. That satisfies procurement evidence.
- 30-minute P1: operationally feasible for a defined subset of endpoints (they must mark which endpoints are "patient-facing" and sign off on the canary runbook). Otherwise P1 remains 1h for unlisted endpoints.
- Credits (high-level conservative approach):
  * Year 1: base crediting per incident up to 1% of monthly invoice
  * Year 2: cap increases to 1.5% if 36-month commit is signed
  * Year 3: 2% cap with same commit
  * These caps avoid large single-month swings yet give visible improvement across the term.

- Concession path: 5% committed discount on seats for 36m + 10% 'response-lane' surcharge waiver in year 1 (we absorb incremental ops cost). After year 1 we step to 50% of that waiver. This keeps TCV steady while giving Luminor immediate operational improvement.

- Critical regression exit clause: propose a safety valve instead of hard 30-day exit: if we hit three P1 regressions in a 90-day window tied to model/regression quality that materially impacts service, Luminor can trigger a 30-day cure period and optional refund cap equal to one month's committed invoice. Legal prefers cure windows over abrupt termination.

I've attached 'proposed_pricing_sheet.xlsx' with simple math (seat tiers, discounts, credit caps). Priyom — can you sanity-check numbers and prepare two redline variants: (A) 36m with concessions above, (B) 12m with a smaller 3% commit discount and year-over-year credit caps unchanged?

Marissa Cole
Director, Commercial Operations | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

Attachments: proposed_pricing_sheet.xlsx

Subject: Re: SLA crediting, canary escalation, and packaging options

Alyssa / Tom —

Thanks for the quick internal alignment. Based on our ops and commercial review here is a concise offer for review: 

Offer (36-month preferred):
- Commitment: 36 months, 50 seats committed
- Discount: 5% on committed seats for term
- Uptime tiers: 99.95% guaranteed for core, 99.9% for non-core
- P1: 30 minutes for listed patient-facing endpoints (must be enumerated in SOW + accepted canary runbook)
- Crediting caps: Year1=1% / Year2=1.5% / Year3=2% of monthly committed invoice
- Escalation evidence: quarterly roster + named escalation contact in SOW
- Critical regression clause: 30-day cure window + refund cap = 1x monthly invoice if three P1 regressions in 90 days

If you accept, we'll: 1) create a short SOW that enumerates patient-facing endpoints and attaches the canary runbook, 2) push the HubSpot deal to final pricing and create a DocuSign packet with the concession paths (link below).

Proposed next steps: Confirm the endpoint list and whether procurement is comfortable with the cure-window approach. If yes, I'll circulate the DocuSign today and target signature by Apr 21.
